code.originalText: Two-week review after sacubitril-valsartan, carvedilol and empagliflozin: kidney function, potassium, angiography result and the next medicine

text.paragraph: Two-week review after starting sacubitril-valsartan, carvedilol and empagliflozin. [S]

Mr. Kahanamoku returns two weeks after starting carvedilol and empagliflozin and twelve days after his first dose of sacubitril-valsartan, taken as planned 36 hours after the last lisinopril. He feels better: he walks up the slope near his office without stopping, the ankle swelling has gone, and he sleeps flat. He has had no lightheadedness, cough, genital itching or burning on passing urine. His home weight is steady at 93.5 to 94 kg. Coronary angiography last week showed an old complete blockage of the main artery at the front of the heart, with collaterals, and only mild narrowing elsewhere; the cardiologist advised that opening it would not help the scarred muscle. He is ready for the second iron infusion. [S]

text.paragraph: Vital signs recorded on 2026-04-13; see the Vital Signs section. [S]

tr.td: Well; blood pressure 118/72, pulse 74; weight 93.6 kg
Regular rhythm; no S3; apical systolic murmur
No edema; right radial access site healed

Breathlessness on exertion for six weeks (paddling out, walking uphill, finishing his morning swim), with ankle swelling by evening and tiredness, five years after a heart attack; cause to be determined
S — Synthetic presenting problem, resolved at the second visit when the echocardiogram and cardiology established heart failure with reduced ejection fraction.
Coronary artery disease with an old anterior myocardial infarction five years ago, treated with medicines; synthetic modern episode linked to the documented heart attack of 1952
S — Synthetic modern diagnosis; the 1952 heart attack remains D in the history.
Heart failure with reduced ejection fraction from ischemic cardiomyopathy (ejection fraction 30% with a thinned, akinetic anterior wall and apex), NYHA class III at diagnosis
S — Synthetic modern diagnosis made at the second visit; no claim that he had heart failure in his lifetime.
Iron deficiency without anemia (ferritin 62 ng/mL, transferrin saturation 16%)
S — Synthetic finding at the heart failure workup.

list.item:
Heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (I50.22). Improving: NYHA class II to III, euvolemic, KCCQ-12 56 from 38. Potassium 4.5 mmol/L and creatinine 1.16 mg/dL (eGFR 69), a 7% rise, expected and acceptable. Blood pressure 118/72 and pulse 74 allow the next steps. [S]
Start spironolactone 12.5 mg daily (potassium below 5.0 and eGFR above 30).
Raise carvedilol to 6.25 mg twice daily.
Continue sacubitril-valsartan 24/26 mg, empagliflozin and furosemide 40 mg.
Metabolic panel at the review in two weeks, one to two weeks after spironolactone.
Sick-day rules reviewed again now that four medicines act on the kidney.

Coronary artery disease (I25.2). Chronic total occlusion of the left anterior descending artery feeding a scarred, thinned wall, with mild disease elsewhere: medical therapy, not revascularization, as the cardiologist advised. [S]
Continue aspirin 81 mg and atorvastatin 80 mg.

Iron deficiency (E61.1). First infusion two weeks ago without reaction. [S]
Second ferric carboxymaltose 750 mg infusion today.
Iron studies at about six months.

text.paragraph: Guideline basis: 2022 AHA/ACC/HFSA Guideline for the Management of Heart Failure (2022); 2024 ACC Expert Consensus Decision Pathway for Treatment of Heart Failure With Reduced Ejection Fraction (2024); 2023 AHA/ACC/ACCP/ASPC/NLA/PCNA Guideline for the Management of Patients With Chronic Coronary Disease (2023); CMID: Clinical Monitoring Intelligence Database, heart failure and ischemic heart disease monographs (2026)

Follow-up: Review in two weeks with a metabolic panel (two weeks after spironolactone), a lipid panel and the KCCQ-12. Call for lightheadedness, vomiting or diarrhea (sick-day rules), or a weight change beyond the plan. Next scheduled visit 2026-04-27: two-week review, five days after the sick visit: kidney function and potassium, medicine doses, lipids, and cardiac rehabilitation adapted to the ocean. [S]
